page: Microsoft Azure D2lds_v6 is a low-memory, local-disk variant within Azure's general-purpose virtual machine lineup, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor built on x86_64 architecture, operating at speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 1 physical core via symmetric multithreading (2 threads per core), alongside a massive 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes modern instruction set support such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography. System memory is constrained at 4.0 GB total (2.0 GB per vCPU), and it features 118 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. There are no GPUs provisioned.

Benchmark results highlight an asymmetry between single-threaded execution and multi-threaded scaling. Due to high clock speeds and architectural improvements, the server delivers strong single-core performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2108.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.39 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput falls in the lower tiers due to the 2-vCPU hardware footprint. Geekbench multi-core registers at 2627.0, and stress-ng multi-core reaches 1984.89. Uncached memory throughput is comparatively low, with large-block memory read bandwidth measured at 21.01 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.28 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the D2lds_v6 offers an entry point for workloads that require fast per-core compute and local NVMe storage without paying for surplus memory capacity. The primary tradeoff centers on memory density: with only 4.0 GB of RAM, workloads that process large in-memory working sets or perform extensive parallel compilation will quickly encounter resource limits, as reflected in low software compilation and database benchmark metrics.

This server instance is best suited for compute-focused background tasks with limited memory footprints, light static web serving, microservices, small automated pipelines, and batch processing that benefits from fast single-threaded performance combined with direct local NVMe temp disk space.
